comparison: Both evaluate the methodological claims (C12, C38, C40, C68-C78) and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate statistical procedures and clear documentation. Peer reviewers acknowledge thorough analysis with clearly reported results, though Reviewer 3 questions interpretation of the GLM framework without challenging the methods themselves.

Both address Bayesian model comparison results (C20, C44). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate methodology. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN - they don't dispute the model comparison result itself, but Reviewer 3 questions whether improved fit reflects distinct neural processes versus utility curvature or model misspecification.

Perfect agreement on parameter correlation claims (C41-C43). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate statistical tests with clear reporting. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge clearly reported statistical significance and thorough analysis, with no challenges to these control analyses.

Both evaluate sensitivity analysis (C25) and find it SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the correlation remains significant despite reduced effect size. Peer reviewers acknowledge the supplementary examination without challenge, supporting the robustness of the main finding.

Both address theoretical interpretations connecting behavioral findings to mechanisms (C53-C56). Both rate UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes reasonable logic but speculative mechanisms. Peer reviewers acknowledge the observation as interesting but note it doesn't explain the covariation and that the composite model is not explanatory.

Both evaluate main conclusions about distractor effects (C29-C31, with peer review also including C46-C48). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED despite noting arbitrary median split. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN - Reviewer 1 finds evidence convincing but notes interpretation questions, while Reviewer 3 extensively critiques the interpretation framework.

OpenEval evaluates robustness checks (C46-C49) as SUPPORTED despite marginal significance in GLM4. Peer review R2 addresses overlapping claims (C46-C48) within broader evaluation of main conclusions, rating UNCERTAIN due to interpretation concerns rather than statistical results themselves.

Both address C49 regarding absolute vs. relative distractor quantification. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED noting consistent directional patterns. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging meticulousness but noting conclusions mostly hold and questioning why impact differs between absolute and relative terms.

Both evaluate foundational claims (C1-C3, with peer review also including C6-C7). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as well-established background. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN - Reviewer 3 fundamentally challenges the premise that choices ought to be unaffected by distractors, questioning the entire normative framework.

Both address theoretical landscape claims (C4-C11). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as accurate literature summary with appropriate context. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, noting forward-looking integration of previous findings, though Reviewer 2 raises generalizability concerns beyond lottery tasks.

Both evaluate neuroanatomical framework claims (C32-C37, with peer review also including C62-C63, C65-C66). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as appropriate prior findings. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 praising excellent connection to previous neural findings and noting potential to motivate new studies.

Both evaluate claims about individual variability in distractor effects (C57-C61, with peer review also including C64, C67). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes accurate literature summary providing important precedent. Peer reviewers acknowledge these as appropriately framed interpretations of existing evidence with excellent synthesis.

OpenEval evaluates anatomically distinct mechanisms claims (C62-C67) as SUPPORTED with strong evidence despite some speculation. Peer review R6 addresses overlapping claims (C62-C63, C65-C66) within broader neuroanatomical evaluation, also rating SUPPORTED and praising connection to previous neural findings.
